standard.title: Locate, collect and record information
standard.description: locate, collect and record information and data from a range of sources, including annotated timelines and maps
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y2 (AC9HS2S02): Students collected from a range of source types and recorded on unscaled timelines and labelled maps.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students locate, collect and record information from a range of sources including annotated timelines and maps using appropriate cartographic conventions.

nodes.label: Locating and evaluating sources
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can locate sources suited to a specific inquiry purpose and begin to assess their usefulness.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two sources suited to a specific inquiry purpose and explain why each is suitable.
nodes.typical_width: Locate historical sources (photographs, interviews, newspapers, digital media, stories, maps); collect information through fieldwork (photographs, sketches, natural objects, interviews, surveys); gather from maps, aerial photographs and satellite images.
wider: Compare sources from different perspectives on the same topic and discuss how perspective affects what sources are created
Investigate how the internet can be used as a source and evaluate reliability of different online sources
nodes.hinge_reason: Source selection is now a distinct skill at Year 3 — without being able to locate appropriate sources, fieldwork and annotation tasks cannot be executed.

response_modes.reason: Source selection requires understanding inquiry purpose — model the reasoning 'I need this type of information, therefore this type of source is best suited'.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two sources suited to an inquiry purpose
Explains why each source is suitable

nodes.label: Annotated timelines and maps with conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can construct and annotate timelines and maps using appropriate cartographic conventions including map symbols, title and north point.
nodes.minimum_width: Construct an annotated map or timeline that includes at least one cartographic convention (title, north point, map symbols, legend).
nodes.typical_width: Sequence local people and events in annotated timelines to show change; acquire and record geographical information by constructing and annotating maps using map symbols, title and north point; create tables and graphs to show patterns.
wider: Compare a student-constructed annotated map with a professionally produced map of the same area and discuss differences in detail and conventions
Create an annotated timeline that includes both written annotations and visual evidence

response_modes.reason: Cartographic conventions (north point, legend, title, scale) require deliberate practice — use scaffolded map-making tasks before expecting independent production.

success_criteria: Constructs an annotated map or timeline
Includes at least one cartographic convention accurately
